learning_objective: 📋 Learn how to act like a data detective! Understand how information is gathered through surveys, censuses, and smart sampling.

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: प्राथमिक आंकड़े (पहली बार खुद इकट्ठा किया गया डेटा)
द्वितीयक आंकड़े (किसी और द्वारा पहले से इकट्ठा किया गया डेटा)
जनगणना (जब पूरी आबादी/समूह के हर एक व्यक्ति से डेटा लिया जाए)
प्रतिदर्श / सैंपल (पूरी आबादी का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाला एक छोटा हिस्सा)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Primary data is collected originally by the investigator (like you asking your classmates their favorite color). It is highly accurate but costs time and money. Secondary data is borrowed from existing sources (like reading a government report). It's quick but may not perfectly fit your need.
A questionnaire is a list of questions. A good one should be short, have simple language, avoid 'leading' questions (questions that force a specific answer), and start from general to specific.

Involves collecting data from EVERY single unit of the population (the 'universe'). The Census of India is done every 10 years. It gives 100% accurate details but is extremely expensive and time-consuming.

Instead of checking everyone, you check a representative group (like tasting one spoon of soup to check the salt). It's cheaper and faster. 'Random sampling' means every item has an equal chance of being selected (like picking names from a hat).

In India, major secondary data comes from the Census of India (demographics) and the NSSO (National Sample Survey Office), which conducts massive sample surveys on employment, poverty, and consumer expenditure.

fun_activity.title: 🍰 The Soup Logic
fun_activity.instructions: If you are cooking a massive pot of soup, do you need to drink the whole pot to know if there is enough salt? No! You stir it well and taste just one spoonful. This is the exact logic behind 'Sampling' in statistics!

exam_tips: 📌 Sampling Error is the difference between the sample result and the true population result. Non-sampling errors occur due to mistakes in recording, biased questions, or non-response.
📌 Distinguish between Personal Interview (interviewer asks questions face-to-face) and Mailed Questionnaire (sent via post/email, respondent fills it).
📌 A 'Pilot Survey' is a pre-test or trial run of the questionnaire on a small group to find out any mistakes before the main survey.
quick_recap: ⭐ The 'Population' or 'Universe' in statistics refers to the totality of all items under study, not just human population.
⭐ Secondary data must be used with caution—always check the reliability and suitability of the source.
⭐ Exit polls during elections are classic examples of the Sample Survey method.
